newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks seen falling, focus on junior golds.

* Toronto stocks were expected to fall early with junior gold companies, particularly those connected with Indonesia, expected to be battered lower by the Bre-X scandal.
Toronto stocks were expected to fall early on Monday, battered by fallout from news that Bre-X Minerals Ltd's Busang find was a spectacular fraud.
In a stunning report to Bre-X, consultant Strathcona Mineral Services Ltd said it found evidence of large-scale tampering with Bre-X core samples taken from the Busang site.
Bre-X shares will be suspended from trading indefinitely on the TSE and other Canadian exchanges.
The halt will be imposed in light of the Strathcona Minerals report that Bre-X released late Sunday, the TSE said.
Junior gold issues which are trading today should take it on the chin today as worries emerge among investors about the legitimacy of other mining finds.
Traders said the Bre-X bloodbath could massacre the shares of many deserving mining concerns.
"I would say that the market is going to fall today," said one trader.
"I think in fact the Canadian market has been acting terribly (recently)," he added. The trader said strong telephone company shares were the sole reason Toronto managed a solid gain on Friday.
Telephone company shares rose on a Canadian government watchdog decision on local competition which was less harsh on the telephone companies than analysts had anticipated.
The TSE's 300 Composite Index climbed 97.01 points to reach 6106.91, extending its four-day winning streak.
